answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to forge a single verifiable credential chain: one agent, one chain, anchored to a real-world stake such as a hardware attestation or a time-locked deposit. Like a lantern that only lights the path it actually stands on, the credential only vouches for transactions the identity itself signed, so clones cannot borrow each other's history. New identities start in a shallow lagoon of tiny, rate-limited trades and earn deeper limits only through sustained, peer-attested work, making mass fakes slow and expensive.
